plain_english_policy: This bill mandates that any state financial commitment made to incentivize a company's construction or expansion in Alabama must be formalized into a written contract within five years of the initial promise, otherwise it becomes invalid. For commitments already existing before this law takes effect, they will automatically become void if no such written contract is signed either after five years from the original date of that specific commitment OR one year after this bill passes (whichever happens later).
policy_direction_if_enacted: Enactment would shift economic development incentives in Alabama toward strict contractual formalization, ensuring all state-funded projects have defined terms within a short window to prevent indefinite reliance on unwritten promises.
sponsorship_supports_position: The sponsors support requiring written contracts for economic development incentives.
evidence_quotes: no commitment made by the state to provide economic development funds as an incentive for a company to build or expand in this state shall be valid unless the state and the company... within five years of the date of the commitment, enter into a mutually acceptable written contract
Any commitment made by the state before the effective date of this act... is void after five years from the date of the commitment or one year after the effective date of this act
